t: Madrid began as a walled military outpost built by the emir Muhammad I in the late 9th century, passed to Alfonso VI of León and Castile in 1083 or 1085, and grew into a middle-ranking town of the Crown of Castile.
Philip II set his court there in June 1561, and from then Madrid was the seat of the monarchy, except between 1601 and 1606, when the court sat at Valladolid and the population fell.

The city rose against French troops on 2 May 1808, was besieged from October 1936 in the Civil War until it fell on 28 March 1939, and was confirmed as the capital by the constitutions of 1931 and 1978.
dyk: When the court went to Valladolid in 1601, Madrid reportedly lost half of its people, and it was won back in 1606 partly by an offer of 250,000 ducats from the town to help pay for the court’s return.
ev: The emir Muhammad I has a citadel built on the left bank of the Manzanares
Alfonso VI of León and Castile takes Madrid, though some historians date the conquest to 1085
Philip II settles his court in Madrid
The court moves to Valladolid and Madrid loses much of its population; it returns in 1606
The people of Madrid rise against the French on 2 May
The Canal de Isabel II brings the waters of the Lozoya to the city
The military rising is defeated in Madrid and the city is besieged until 1939
The new constitution confirms Madrid as the capital of Spain

f.founded: A citadel built by the Umayyad emir Muhammad I of Córdoba in the second half of the 9th century, dated to between 852 and 886; Christian conquest in 1083 or 1085.
f.where: On the left bank of the Manzanares river in the central part of the Iberian peninsula, on the southern Meseta Central about 60 kilometres south of the Guadarrama mountains, in Spain.
f.known: The emirate fortress of Majriṭ; conquest by Alfonso VI; the court of Philip II from 1561; the Siglo de Oro of Cervantes, Lope de Vega and Velázquez; the Dos de Mayo uprising of 1808; the Civil War siege of 1936 to 1939; the Prado and the Royal Palace
f.today: Madrid is the capital and largest city of Spain and of the autonomous community of Madrid, with over 3.4 million people in the city proper.
